clues.text: This town sits in the heart of its land, high up in the Andes. It stands on a high flat plain in the east part of the range.
clues.narrowing: Puts the player on a high Andean plateau in northern South America.

source.quote: The city is located in the center of Colombia, on a high plateau known as the Bogotá savanna, part of the Altiplano Cundiboyacense located in the Eastern Cordillera of the Andes.

clues.text: High in the mountains, the climate stays cool and even all year. Dry seasons and rainy seasons take turns.
clues.narrowing: Keeps a cool highland city where the weather barely changes with the seasons.

source.quote: Bogotá features a subtropical highland climate with uniform precipitation (Köppen: Cfb, Trewartha: Cfll).

clues.text: On 6 Aug 1538, a man from Spain set up this town as the chief town of a new realm. He had marched through the Andes and won the land in hard fights.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to capitals founded by a conquistador in 1538.

source.quote: Bogotá was founded as the capital of the New Kingdom of Granada on 6 August 1538 by Spanish conquistador Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada after a harsh expedition into the Andes conquering the Muisca, the indigenous inhabitants of the Altiplano.

clues.text: A hall in this town holds more old gold than any place on earth. It guards 35,000 bits of gold, and 30,000 more works in stone, clay, and cloth.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital's Gold Museum holds the world's largest pre-Columbian gold collection.

source.quote: The Gold Museum, with 35,000 pieces of tumbaga gold, along with 30,000 objects in ceramic, stone and textiles, represents the largest collection of pre-Columbian gold in the world.

clues.text: Colombia is run from this town, the seat of rule for the whole land. More folk live here than in any other town in the land by far.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: capital and largest city of Colombia.

source.quote: Bogotá is the capital and largest city of Colombia.

reveal.blurb: This city was founded high in the Andes in 1538, after a harsh trek into the mountains. Its Gold Museum guards the world's biggest collection of ancient gold — tens of thousands of shining pieces. Bogotá is the capital of Colombia.
